title: Bouchaud-Inspired Firm Fragility with Optimal Firms
research_question: Can financial fragility, defaults and employment cascades from Bouchaud-inspired macro ABMs be reconstructed with optimizing firms and clearing credit, goods and labor markets?
feasibility_hypothesis: Conditional: Mark-0-style heuristic behavioral rules are not automatically optimizing general equilibrium; compare the original heuristic benchmark to a separately microfounded firm model.
mechanisms: Heterogeneous firm investment, employment and financing
Credit supply, collateral and endogenous default
Entry, exit and propagation of balance-sheet shocks
state_variables: firm net worth, debt, employment and productivity
required_equations: Firm dynamic optimization and default/limited-liability constraints
Intermediary budget and loan market clearing
Household ownership and distribution of profits/losses
Aggregate resource and labor market clearing
comparison_baseline: Stage 0/4 equilibrium without frictions; original Bouchaud-style heuristic ABM as a labeled non-equilibrium comparator
acceptance_tests: Firm and bank ledger reconciliation after default
No double count of credit, capital or dividend flows
Shock-induced tipping region stable across solvers and grids
stage_gate: Accept only an explicitly optimized firm/credit mechanism; document which original Bouchaud properties do and do not survive.
reference_leads: Bouchaud and coauthors on Mark-0 macroeconomics
Corporate default and financial accelerator literature

implementation.method: equilibrium solving plus ABM/distribution verification when relevant
implementation.language: Julia proposed; environment and APIs to be verified before implementation
